To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

reggie‐deficient (reggie‐1 k. o.) mouse hippocampal (CA1) neurons in culture suffer from impaired cargo (PSD‐95, Ncadherin, AMPAR, and NMDAR) trafficking, spine synapses formation, and in vitro LTP‐related AMPAR surface exposure.
reggie-1 and -2 (flotillin-1 and flotillin-2) participate in Rab-11a dependent cargo trafficking, spine-synapse formation, and LTP-related exposure of AMPA receptors (GluA) at the neuronal surface.

Reggie‐1 and Reggie‐2 (flotillin‐1 and ‐ 2) and Rab11A participate in the trafficking of postsynapse‐related cargo, spine synapse development, and the in vitro LTP correlate in hippocampal mouse neurons
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of reggie-1 and -2 in the formation and function of spine synapses in mouse hippocampi.
the role of reggies and Rab in the regulation of the trafficking of postsynaptically relevant proteins and in the formation of spine synapses in the mouse hippocampus.
the regulation of synaptic function and plasticity by the recycling endosome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data presented in the manuscript show that reggies are important for the development of synapses and for the induction of long-term potentiation in hippocampal neuron.
reggie-1 and -2 (flotillin-1 and - 2) are involved in spine synapse formation.
Reggie-1 and reggies-2 participate in Rab11A dependent cargo trafficking, spine synaptic formation and LTP related AMPA receptor (gluA1) surface exposition in mouse hippocampinal neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reggie‐deficiency causes a trafficking‐related defect that affects spine synapse formation in vitro and the in vitro LTP correlate.
reggie‐deficiency impairs spine‐directed cargo trafficking and spine synapse formation.
the reggies and Rab‐11a are involved in the trafficking of postsynapse proteins, such as PSD‐95, and in the formation of the postsynaptic density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reggie‐flotillin proteins and Rab11a function together in the trafficking of PSD‐ 95, N‐ cadherin, Glutamate Receptor (GluA)1 and GluA2 to spine synapses, and in the in vitro correlate to LTP.

reggie-1 and -2 function at Rab1a recycling containers in trafficking of PSD-95, N-cadherin, Glutamate receptor subunit 1 (GluA) and Glutamate NMDA receptor 1 (GlnN) to spine synapses and promote (togethers with other signaling molecules) the formation of spine synapses, the in vitro correlate to long term potentiation (LPT) and LTP itself.
reggie-1 (Flot2) and reggie- 2 (Flot1) participate in Rab-11a-dependent cargo (including PSD-95, N-cadherin, and GluA1) trafficking, spine synapses formation and the in-vitro correlate of LTP.
